source_name: ICZ Group — Aktuality (Czech newsroom)
why_relevant: Dated Czech-language news stream (items observed through July 2026) covering product launches, certifications and events. ICZ is diversified into ATM/air-traffic, logistics and public sector, so banking items are sparse — but the feed is the vendor's only chronological disclosure channel and is where a bank-project announcement would first appear. Czech is the primary language with EN and SK mirrors.

source_name: Avenga — Success stories and News (successor domain of Cleverlance)
why_relevant: IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE CELL BRIEF: www.cleverlance.com issues a 301 redirect to www.avenga.com, not to Aricoma. Cleverlance's Czech banking-integration practice therefore has to be tracked through Avenga, which retains Prague, Brno and Ostrava offices and lists financial clients including Raiffeisen Bank, UniCredit, Generali, Fidelity, Bank of Cyprus and Marginalen Bank. Missing this redirect would leave a large slice of Czech bank-IT delivery history uncovered.

source_name: Unicorn — corporate site and news archive (unicorn.com)
why_relevant: Unicorn (tagline 'Tvorime digitalni budoucnost') is a major Czech software house with long-running banking delivery. Its sitemap confirms a full trilingual structure (root, /en/, /cs/) with ~168 URLs, a news archive (news-archiv-unicorn-all, news-detail) and product pages for Unicorn Universe, but NO dedicated case-study/reference section and NO investor-relations section were present in the sitemap. The site is client-side rendered, so plain HTTP fetches return only the title element — collection needs a headless browser.

source_name: Asseco Central Europe — corporate site / newsroom
why_relevant: Asseco Central Europe is a core-banking and financial-software supplier across CZ/SK and the single most important named actor in this cell for core-system disclosure. The legacy domain www.asseco-ce.com issues a 302 to ce.asseco.com, confirming the domain migration. Both ce.asseco.com/ and ce.asseco.com/en/news/ returned HTTP 403 to a plain fetch — the strong hypothesis is bot defence (WAF/Cloudflare) on a live site, NOT a dead host. Do not record as dead; re-attempt with a browser-grade client.

source_name: Asseco Poland — Investor Relations (listed parent of Asseco Central Europe)
why_relevant: Asseco Poland is WSE-listed and consolidates the Central Europe segment, so its periodic and current reports are the only audited, regulator-grade financial disclosure touching Czech banking-software revenue in this cell. Segment notes and management commentary are where Czech banking-sector performance would be quantified. Not yet reachable: https://asseco.com/investor-relations/ and https://inwestor.asseco.com/en/ both returned HTTP 403 to plain fetch — again a bot-defence hypothesis, not a dead-site verdict.

source_name: GEM System — corporate site
why_relevant: Named seed actor for this cell (Czech IT services with financial-sector delivery). Could not be characterised: https://www.gemsystem.cz/, https://gemsystem.cz/, https://www.gemsystem.cz/cz/ and https://www.gemsystem.cz/robots.txt all terminated with 'too many redirects (exceeded 10)'. That pattern usually indicates a misconfigured www/non-www or language-cookie redirect loop against a cookieless client, or a locale negotiation loop — the host resolves and responds, so it is very likely live. Retain as a target and re-attempt with cookie support.

source_name: CCA Group — Reference and Novinky
why_relevant: Named seed actor, verified live with a clean Czech structure (/reference/, /novinky/, /o-spolecnosti/, service pages for custom software, application maintenance, customer support and cybersecurity; 100+ staff, 30+ years). However its published references are public-sector and industrial — Ministry of Justice information systems since 1995, the Czech Office for Surveying and Cadastre, the Ministry of Finance gambling-oversight system AISG, and SKODA JS ERP — with no banking clients visible. Keep at low-frequency monitoring: it is a plausible bidder on state-owned bank work but is not currently a bank-technology disclosure channel.

source_name: SystemOnLine.cz — IT pro banky a financni organizace (vertical) + IT vendor directory
why_relevant: The single best Czech-language pointer source for this cell. SystemOnLine (publisher of the IT Systems magazine) runs a dedicated banking/financial-organisations vertical that republishes vendor case studies and bylined vendor articles, AND maintains a supplier directory (dodavatele IT sluzeb a reseni) plus product overviews covering 77+ ERP and 51+ CRM vendors. That directory is the snowball engine for discovering bank-IT vendors outside the ten seed actors. Note the bare domain systemonline.cz fails TLS hostname validation — always use the www host.

source_name: Bankovnictvi (casopis) — Technologie section
why_relevant: The Czech banking trade magazine (published by 4H production s.r.o., Prague) with a standing Technologie rubric alongside Banky a finance, Produkty a sluzby, Regulace, Rozhovory and Personalie. It is the demand-side mirror of the vendor newsrooms in this cell: where a vendor claims a win, Bankovnictvi often carries the bank's own framing, plus executive interviews and personnel moves that identify the decision-makers behind technology spend. Freemium — free previews with a subscription tier.

source_name: Computertrends.cz (successor of Computerworld.cz, IDG/iinfo network)
why_relevant: Czech IT-professional daily ('Denik pro IT profesionaly') carrying a Press Room stream of vendor announcements plus analysis (/analyzy-a-studie/) and security (/securityworld/) sections. Note the domain migration: www.computerworld.cz now issues a 301 to www.computertrends.cz — any historical link set pointing at computerworld.cz needs rewriting. Useful as a secondary confirmation channel when a vendor claims a bank project, and for catching smaller integrators that never issue their own press release.

source_name: ICT UNIE — member register of Czech IT and electronic-communications firms
why_relevant: Czech ICT trade association ('Profesni sdruzeni firem z oboru IT informacnich technologii a elektronickych komunikaci') publishing a member list of roughly 60 companies with logos, an Aktuality stream, a 'V mediich' clippings section, working groups and sector statistics drawn from the Czech Statistical Office. This is the cheapest way to complete the vendor actor map beyond the ten seed names and to pick up the sector-level aggregates that contextualise individual vendor wins.

source_name: Hlidac statu — aggregated contracts, tenders and subsidies with API/MCP access
why_relevant: Independent Czech watchdog (self-described as the country's largest, 10 years running, donor-funded, no state money or advertising) that indexes 8.5m contracts, 1.5m public tenders, subsidies and official salaries. Its value over the raw Registr smluv is queryability and entity resolution: it offers a documented API (api.hlidacstatu.cz) and an MCP server endpoint (mcp.api.hlidacstatu.cz), all free of charge. This is the practical way to run standing supplier-side queries for Asseco, Trask, Adastra, ICZ, Unicorn, CCA, Aricoma and Profinit against every public counterparty at once.

source_name: NEN / NIPEZ — Narodni elektronicky nastroj (public procurement) and ISVZ statistics
why_relevant: The national electronic tool for administering and publishing Czech public contracts and concessions, reporting 22,486 contracting authorities, 41,555 suppliers, 269,324 realised contracts and CZK 2,119bn in value. It links to the Vestnik verejnych zakazek (procurement gazette) and to ISVZ statistical reporting at isvz.nipez.cz/reporty. Directly relevant to this cell wherever a state-owned or public financial institution procures banking technology, and it also yields supplier-side profiles for the seed vendors, revealing public-sector revenue concentration that private vendors do not otherwise disclose.

source_name: Temenos — Press Releases & News Centre
why_relevant: Temenos is the single most CZ-relevant global core-banking vendor: Komercni banka (Societe Generale group) selected Temenos Transact and went live on it, and both events were announced ONLY on the vendor's global English newsroom, not by the Czech bank in Czech. The listing exposes ~488 releases with structured filters for Region (Europe), Category (Press Releases / Customer News / Financial / Ad-hoc / Analyst Report), Solution, Topic, Year and Month, which makes a durable, low-noise standing collection target for Czech customer-win detection.

source_name: Temenos — Customer Success Story library
why_relevant: Case-study format carries detail that press releases omit: modules deployed, implementation partner, timeline, migration scope. A Komercni banka success story exists, which is the richest single English-language description of a Czech core-banking programme available from any vendor. Case studies are also refreshed asynchronously from the press cycle, so they catch deployments that were never press-released.

source_name: Temenos — Investor Relations (ad-hoc announcements, results, financial calendar)
why_relevant: SIX-listed issuer, so ad-hoc disclosure obligations force out material client and financial events on a fixed calendar. Results presentations and half-year/annual reports are where regional revenue mix and named marquee clients (including CEE) surface, and the quarterly earnings call is the channel where a Czech deployment gets referenced as proof-point without a standalone press release. The IR area exposes a dedicated ad-hoc feed via a category-filtered press-release URL.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf — Investor Relations press release archive
why_relevant: Diebold Nixdorf routes ALL corporate press releases through its IR subdomain rather than a marketing newsroom, so this is the canonical announcement channel for ATM/self-service wins including any Czech bank contract. The listing carries a Year selector plus a Category filter (All / Company / Banking / Financial / Retail), and 'Banking' is the exact cut that isolates deployment announcements from earnings noise.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf — SEC filings index
why_relevant: 10-K/10-Q/8-K text is the one place a vendor must describe country exposure, legal entities and material contracts in a form it cannot walk back. Diebold Nixdorf operates a Czech legal entity and CEE service organisation; segment/geography notes and risk factors are a reliable, calendar-driven read on whether CZ is growing or shrinking for the vendor. Also the cleanest cross-check on press-release spin.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf — Banking case studies (region-filterable)
why_relevant: Verified live and clearly CEE-active: the current set includes Cooperative Bank of Kielce (Poland) and Banca Raiffeisen Locarno (Switzerland), i.e. exactly the tier of European bank that would also be a Czech reference. The library has Topic / Media Type / Region filters. No Czech customer appears today, which is itself a competitive-positioning signal worth tracking over time.

source_name: NCR Atleos — Corporate newsroom
why_relevant: The world's largest ATM-as-a-Service and ATM estate operator, and the most likely vendor to announce a Czech outsourcing or ATM-fleet deal. The newsroom is deep (83 pages of items) and mixes NCR Atleos press releases with republished third-party trade coverage, which doubles it as a pointer into ATM Marketplace, Credit Union Business News and similar outlets. Filters: Category (Banking / Company / Enterprise Network Services / Retail banking), Year (2026 back to 2018 and prior) and Type (News article / News release).

source_name: NCR Atleos — Investor Relations press releases (with RSS)
why_relevant: Machine-collectable: a genuine RSS feed exists at /news-events/press-releases/rss, plus stable numeric detail URLs (/detail/<id>/<slug>), a Year and Category (All / Financial) filter, an SEC filings index and an IR calendar. This is the highest-automation-value endpoint in the whole cell. IMPORTANT DURABILITY FLAG: the listing shows 'Shareholders Overwhelmingly Vote to Approve Brink's Acquisition of NCR Atleos' (Jun 30, 2026), so this IR domain is likely to be retired or redirected into Brink's IR — the monitor must be re-pointed and the archive mirrored before that happens.

source_name: NCR Atleos — Insights / Customer Stories library
why_relevant: Filterable by ATM as a Service, ATM Security, Branch Transformation, Cash Optimization, Fleet Modernization, Payments Modernization and Retail ATM Network — the exact solution taxonomy a Czech bank would buy against. Currently overwhelmingly US credit-union content with Santander UK as the only European reference and no Czech customer, which is a usable competitive-white-space signal.

source_name: FIS — Media Room
why_relevant: FIS press releases are the announcement channel for core, payments and treasury deals in EMEA, and the Media Room additionally curates third-party coverage (Forbes, WSJ), so it works as a pointer into tier-1 press as well. Stable, date-partitioned release URL pattern /about-us/media-room/press-release/<year>/<slug> makes historical backfill cheap.

source_name: FIS — Investor Relations
why_relevant: Quarterly results, 10-K/10-Q and earnings-call material for a vendor whose EMEA banking-solutions segment covers CZ. Earnings-call Q&A is a recognised channel for naming country wins that never get a dedicated press release, and the transcript is the only place some CEE colour appears.

source_name: Fiserv — Newsroom
why_relevant: Fiserv is a top-tier global payments and account-processing vendor whose Clover/merchant-acquiring push into Europe makes Czech merchant and bank partnerships plausible; announcements land on the standalone newsroom subdomain rather than fiserv.com. Confirmed as the canonical newsroom by a 302 redirect from https://www.fiserv.com/en/about-fiserv/newsroom.html to https://newsroom.fiserv.com/newsroom.

source_name: Finastra — Press & Media
why_relevant: Finastra covers lending, treasury, payments hubs and universal banking in EMEA and regularly announces named European bank customers in English only. Named explicitly in the cell scope; must be tracked even though this pass could not read the listing.

source_name: Auriga — News & Media (with RSS feed)
why_relevant: Auriga (WWS multivendor ATM software) is the closest competitive analogue to Printec's software positioning in CEE. Verified live with a working RSS feed at /en/feed/, 5+ pages of archive, EN/IT/ES language versions and a clear /en/news-and-media/news/<slug>/ pattern. Current geographic footprint on the newsroom shows Madrid, London, Dubai and Poland but NO Czech Republic — a directly usable competitor-positioning datapoint, and a tripwire for the moment that changes.

source_name: Thales Cyber & Digital (CPL) — Newsroom
why_relevant: This is the Thales business unit that owns payShield HSMs, payment card issuance and digital identity — the Thales assets that actually touch Czech banks and card personalisation. Verified live with ~9 pages of archive, a companion third-party-coverage page at /about-us/in-the-news and a newsletter subscription. Distinct from the Thales Group corporate press room, which is dominated by defence and aerospace noise.

source_name: Thales Group — corporate press releases (journalist area)
why_relevant: Group-level channel for material contracts and for the Thales Czech Republic entity; complements the CPL newsroom, which does not carry group-level or country-organisation announcements. Low signal-to-noise for banking (defence-heavy) but needed for completeness on the Thales side of the cell.

source_name: Printec Group — News / newsroom
why_relevant: Printec is the named regional benchmark in this cell and operates a Czech subsidiary; its group newsroom is where CEE wins, partnerships (Diebold Nixdorf, NCR, Auriga-class software) and country-organisation news are published in English. Needed both as a peer-tracking source and as the reference point against which the global vendors' Czech claims are compared.

source_name: Comarch — Financial Services news (CEE-focused)
why_relevant: Comarch is the most credible CEE-headquartered comparable to the global vendors: Polish, listed, and explicitly building 'corporate banking presence in the CEE region' per its own award announcements. Verified live with 35 pages of archive back to 2008, a Year filter and EN/PL/DE/FR/IT/ES/PT language editions. Its Czech-market moves are a leading indicator for regional vendor competition.

source_name: SEC EDGAR full-text search (vendor filings filtered for Czech references)
why_relevant: The single highest-leverage cross-vendor instrument in this cell: one query surfaces every Czech mention across the 10-K/10-Q/8-K text of Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, FIS, Fiserv, Global Payments, Euronet Worldwide and ACI Worldwide simultaneously — subsidiary lists (Exhibit 21), geographic segment notes, material contracts and risk factors. Unlike newsrooms it is mandatory, dated, and cannot be quietly deleted.

source_name: ATM Marketplace (Networld Media Group) — ATM & self-service trade press
why_relevant: The industry wire that global ATM vendors themselves republish (NCR Atleos syndicates ATM Marketplace pieces into its own newsroom), so it functions as a cross-vendor aggregator: one feed catches Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Auriga, Hyosung, KAL and Euronet announcements without polling each newsroom. Verified live with an RSS feed at /rss/ and a searchable supplier directory at /companies/directory/ that is itself a pointer to further vendor actors. Coverage skews North American, so treat European hit-rate as moderate.

source_name: Finextra — fintech and banking-technology wire
why_relevant: Finextra publishes vendor press releases verbatim alongside editorial and is the default European distribution channel for Temenos, Finastra, FIS, ACI and Backbase announcements — including ones that never appear prominently on the vendor's own site. It is the most reliable single fallback for the vendors in this cell whose own newsrooms are WAF-blocked (Finastra, Printec).

source_name: ČTK Protext — Czech press-release distribution wire (finance and IT categories)
why_relevant: MANDATORY LOCAL-LANGUAGE COUNTERPART TO THIS CELL. Protext is the Czech News Agency's paid press-release distribution service: when an international vendor or its Czech bank customer wants a Czech-language announcement to reach Czech media, it goes through here, and the item is archived in ČTK's Infobanka and syndicated to 15+ Czech news portals. Verified live and genuinely carrying financial-sector releases from Komerční banka among others. This is the channel on which a Czech-language mirror of a global vendor's English announcement would appear — the direct test of the cell's core hypothesis that vendors announce in EN what the Czech customer never confirms locally.

source_name: Bankovnictví online (časopis Bankovnictví, 4H production s.r.o.)
why_relevant: The Czech banking trade magazine, with a dedicated Technologie section and an explicit commercial-supplement model (komerční přílohy) that vendors buy — meaning international vendors' Czech-market messaging surfaces here in Czech, often naming the bank. It is the domestic mirror against which an English global-newsroom claim can be corroborated or shown to be locally unacknowledged. Sections verified: /banky-finance, /aktuality, /komentare, /rozhovory, /prilohy, plus Regulace, Technologie, Produkty a služby, Eventy, Personálie.

source_name: IT Systems / SystemOnLine.cz — Czech enterprise-IT trade portal (Banky a finanční organizace section)
why_relevant: Verified live Czech IT trade portal with an explicit 'Banky a finanční organizace' vertical, a vendor/product directory ('Přehledy'), and a publishing model that mixes original analysis with vendor press releases. This is where an international banking-technology vendor's Czech partner or local subsidiary places technical-market content in Czech, and the vendor directory doubles as a pointer for expanding the CZ vendor actor map beyond the global names in this cell.

source_name: Euronet Worldwide — corporate news and investor relations
why_relevant: Euronet is structurally the most Czech-exposed listed player in this cell: it runs a very large independent ATM estate and processing operation in the Czech Republic and has long-standing Czech operational roots, so its 10-K geography notes, quarterly ATM-count disclosures and press releases are a direct read on the Czech cash and self-service market that no Czech bank publishes. Treat as a top-tier target once the correct live path is established.

source_name: Syncordis (Temenos implementation partner) — snowballed actor, delivery-side channel
why_relevant: Snowballed directly from the verified Komerční banka press release, which names Syncordis as the implementation partner that delivered the Temenos Transact go-live in under 12 months. Implementation and SI partners are a systematically under-watched channel: they publish project detail, headcount and phase-completion news that the software vendor and the bank both omit, and the partner directory itself expands the actor map (SIs, regional resellers) for every vendor in this cell. The named partner is the concrete lead; the vendor partner directory is the reusable pointer.

source_name: Česká bankovní asociace (ČBA) — Členové / Members registry
why_relevant: Server-rendered roster of ČBA member banks — the cheapest near-complete enumeration of licensed banks and foreign bank branches operating in CZ, including building societies (ČSOB Stavební spořitelna, Modrá pyramida, Raiffeisen stavební spořitelna, Stavební spořitelna ČS) and state banks (ČEB, Národní rozvojová banka). Observed ~33 entries incl. Air Bank, AS Inbank odštěpný závod, Banka CREDITAS, Bank of China (CEE), BNP Paribas pobočka, Citibank Europe, COMMERZBANK pobočka Praha, Česká spořitelna, ČSOB, Deutsche Bank Filiale Prag, Fio banka, HSBC Continental Europe, ICBC Prague Branch, ING Bank N.V., J&T BANKA, Komerční banka, mBank organizační složka, MONETA Money Bank, Oberbank AG, Partners Banka, PKO BP Czech Branch, PPF banka, Raiffeisenbank, TRINITY BANK, UniCredit Bank CZ&SK, VÚB pobočka Praha. Each name is a seed for A1 disclosure/IR/annual-report tracking. An English mirror exists at /about-us/members.

source_name: ČBA Monitor — banking sector & macro statistics portal
why_relevant: ČBA's dedicated statistics/analysis property, distinct from the main association site. Publishes headline sector aggregates (observed: banking sector assets ~11,911 bn CZK, sector headcount 37,919, 43 banks by size band, sector profits), macro indicators, credit and deposit series, property prices, the ČBA macroeconomic forecast (ČBA Prognóza) and economist commentary. This is the single best free aggregated view of the Czech banking sector's size and direction, and it names the bank economists who front it — useful for A1 earnings/disclosure context and for sourcing quotable sector baselines.

source_name: ČBA Hypomonitor — mortgage market monthly series
why_relevant: The ČBA Hypomonitor is the de-facto reference series for Czech mortgage volumes and average mortgage rates, compiled from member-bank submissions and released monthly with a press release. It is the most frequently cited private-sector banking dataset in CZ media and is the cleanest recurring datapoint tying individual banks' retail lending momentum to sector totals — high value for A1 earnings and disclosure triangulation.

source_name: ČBA — Výroční zprávy (annual reports archive)
why_relevant: Archive of ČBA annual reports as PDFs, with publication dates observed spanning 2011 through 2026-05-26 — sixteen editions. Association annual reports summarise the year's sector aggregates, regulatory files the association fought, working-group output and the member roster as of that year, which makes them the best retrospective series for reconstructing how the Czech banking sector's structure and agenda changed over time.

source_name: ČBA — Zpravodajský servis / články (news & commentary stream)
why_relevant: ČBA's article stream (/clanky/*) carries association press releases, macro commentary, consumer-protection and cyber-security campaigns, and survey write-ups. The sitemap exposes 2,838 URLs of which 704 are /clanky/ items — a complete, crawlable back-catalogue that the JS-rendered front page hides. This is the practical entry point for ČBA press-release monitoring given the site's client-side navigation.

source_name: ČBA — Slovník bankovních pojmů (Czech banking terminology glossary)
why_relevant: The bulk of ČBA's sitemap (roughly 2,100 of 2,838 URLs) is a one-term-per-page Czech banking glossary covering everything from 'zúčtovací systém' and 'zaknihovaný cenný papír' to 'zpráva auditora' and 'zlatá kreditní karta'. For a source-scouting workstream this is a ready-made, authoritative cs<->en terminology corpus for building the local-language query glossary that all other cells depend on — an indirect but high-leverage asset.

source_name: Sdružení pro bankovní karty (SBK) — card market statistics
why_relevant: SBK is the Czech bank card association and this page is the single richest free source on the Czech cards market: downloadable quarterly and full-year card statistics with a year grid running from 2001 to 2026, plus chart series for number of payment cards, cashless transaction counts and volumes, ATM withdrawals, cashback at merchants, e-shop transactions and the merchant-payments-vs-ATM-withdrawal ratio. Critically it also publishes the roster of contributing institutions and a dated changelog of who stopped contributing and why — an implicit, auditable record of Czech card-market exits and consolidations (Zuno into Raiffeisenbank 2017, CCS 2022, Sberbank 04/2022, Diners Club 10/2022, Cofidis 10/2022, Equa Bank into Raiffeisenbank 11/2022, Hello Bank 04/2023, Citibank 01/2024).

source_name: SBK — members-only data area (data.bankovnikarty.cz)
why_relevant: The 'Pro členy' gateway behind which SBK holds the granular member-only card data that the public summary tables aggregate. Worth documenting as a known-existing but gated tier: it defines the ceiling of what free collection can reach and is the thing to request if a paid/associate membership is ever justified.

source_name: Czech cards & payments event circuit (Card Forum, Card Session, Prague Payments Week, Acquiring Day)
why_relevant: The SBK ecosystem runs a cluster of recurring industry events — Card Forum, Card Session, Prague Payments Week, Acquiring Day, plus the Contactless Hockey / Winter Classic sponsor activations. Conference agendas and speaker lists are among the cheapest ways to learn which executives own which payments initiatives, which vendors are selling into Czech banks, and what roadmap items get disclosed off the record before they reach an annual report. Treat as a pointer into people and vendors rather than a data source.
